The first season of the American fantasy drama television series A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms was originally broadcast on HBO between January and February 2026. Based on the Tales of Dunk and Egg written by George R. R. Martin, the series is set approximately 90 years before the events of Game of Thrones. The first season, based on the 1998 novella The Hedge Knight, follows Ser Duncan "Dunk" the Tall (Peter Claffey), a lowborn hedge knight, and his young squire Prince Aegon "Egg" Targaryen (Dexter Sol Ansell) as they participate in a tournament in which Dunk becomes embroiled in a trial.
Among the supporting cast are Daniel Ings as Ser Lyonel Baratheon, a nobleman; Shaun Thomas as Raymun Fossoway, a squire; Tanzyn Crawford as Tanselle, a puppeteer; Danny Webb as Ser Arlan of Pennytree, Dunk's mentor; and Bertie Carvel, Sam Spruell, Finn Bennett, and Henry Ashton as Princes Baelor, Maekar, Aerion, and Daeron Targaryen. The season had a lower budget than its predecessors, and the team filmed the six episodes in Belfast between June and September 2024. Martin, creator of the A Song of Ice and Fire saga on which the franchise is based, collaborated with showrunner Ira Parker on writing the scripts. Dan Romer composed the soundtrack, marking the first time that a season of the franchise did not feature Ramin Djawadi.
A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms received critical acclaim, with praise for the cast's performances, the strength of the script, the production design, and the soundtrack; various media outlets ranked it among the best series of 2026. In the United States, the premiere attracted 6.7 million viewers during its first three days, combining linear viewers and streams on HBO Max, making it the network's third-largest launch in that period. By February, the series averaged 14 million viewers per episode in the United States and 24 million worldwide, making it the third most successful debut season in HBO history.
Cast and characters
Main
* Peter Claffey as Ser Duncan "Dunk" the Tall, a lowborn hedge knight
* Dexter Sol Ansell as Prince Aegon "Egg" Targaryen, a child whom Dunk takes as his squire
Recurring
* Daniel Ings as Ser Lyonel Baratheon, a knight known as the "Laughing Storm" and the heir to House Baratheon of Storm's End
* Shaun Thomas as Raymun Fossoway, Steffon's cousin and squire
* Tanzyn Crawford as Tanselle, a Dornish puppeteer
* Danny Webb as Ser Arlan of Pennytree, an old hedge knight and Dunk's mentor
* Henry Ashton as Prince Daeron "The Drunken" Targaryen, Egg's eldest brother
* Daniel Monks as Ser Manfred Dondarrion, a knight of House Dondarrion of Blackhaven
* Tom Vaughan-Lawlor as Plummer, the steward of Ashford
* Rowan Robinson as Red, a prostitute in Manfred's service
* Edward Ashley as Ser Steffon Fossoway, a knight of House Fossoway of Cider Hall
* Danny Collins as Ser Humfrey Beesbury, a knight of House Beesbury of Honeyholt
* Ross Anderson as Ser Humfrey Hardyng, a knight of House Hardyng
* Bertie Carvel as Prince Baelor "Breakspear" Targaryen, Prince of Dragonstone, Hand of the King and Protector of the Realm, heir to the Iron Throne, and Egg's uncle
* Sam Spruell as Prince Maekar "The Anvil" Targaryen, Prince of Summerhall, Baelor's younger brother, and the father of Daeron, Aerion, and Egg
* Finn Bennett as Prince Aerion "Brightflame" Targaryen, Egg's older brother
* Youssef Kerkour as Steely Pate, a blacksmith hailing from the Reach
* Steve Wall as Lord Leo "Longthorn" Tyrell, lord of Highgarden and head of House Tyrell
* Paul Hunter as Lord Ashford, lord of Ashford and head of House Ashford, who hosts a tournament to celebrate his daughter's name day
* Cara Harris as Lady Gwin Ashford, the young daughter of Lord Ashford
* Oscar Morgan as Prince Valarr Targaryen, Baelor's son
* Wade Briggs as Ser Roland Crakehall, a member of Daeron II's Kingsguard
* Bill Ward as Ser Donnel of Duskendale, a member of Daeron II's Kingsguard
* Russell Simpson as Lord Medgar Tully, lord of Riverrun and head of House Tully
* William Houston as Ser Robyn Rhysling, a one-eyed knight of House Rhysling
Guest
* Bamber Todd portrays young Dunk
* Carla Harrison-Hodge as Beony, a prostitute in Manfred's service
* Chloe Lea as Rafe, Dunk's childhood friend
* Edward Davis as Alester, a member of the City Watch of King's Landing

| ShortSummary    = Dunk buries his deceased mentor, Ser Arlan of Pennytree. Taking Arlan's sword, shield, and three horses, Dunk travels to a tournament being held in Ashford. At an inn, a belligerent drunk noble says he dreamed of Dunk. A bald child that Dunk believes is the stable boy asks to be his squire for the tournament, but Dunk refuses. Dunk meets Plummer, Ashford's steward, and requests to enter the tournament by claiming that Arlan knighted him before dying. Plummer says someone must vouch for him. Dunk seeks out Ser Manfred Dondarrion, whose father Arlan served. Two prostitutes, Beony and Red, mock Dunk for his ragged appearance and claim Manfred is unavailable, before sympathizing with him. Dunk meets Ser Steffon Fossoway and befriends his squire, Raymun Fossoway, before watching a puppet show featuring a fire-breathing dragon puppet performed by Tanselle. Raymun takes Dunk to Ser Lyonel Baratheon's feast; Dunk befriends Lyonel, who doubts his tournament chances. Dunk finds Manfred, who refuses to vouch for him. Back at his campsite, Dunk re-encounters the bald child, who calls himself Egg; Dunk names himself Ser Duncan the Tall and makes Egg his squire. They see a shooting star, which Egg claims will bring good luck.

| ShortSummary    = Dunk eulogizes Arlan to numerous participants at the tournament, including Lord Leo Tyrell, though none remembers Arlan serving them. Dunk witnesses the Targaryen princes Baelor, Maekar, and Aerion arriving. The Kingsguard Ser Roland Crakehall and Ser Donnel of Duskendale jest with Dunk about knighthood. Dunk sneaks into Ashford's castle and overhears that two of Maekar's sons, Daeron and Aegon, are missing. He asks the Targaryens to vouch for him. Baelor remembers Arlan and vouches for Dunk, but advises he create his own coat of arms. Dunk and Egg watch Tanselle perform. Infatuated, Dunk asks Tanselle if she will paint a new coat of arms on his shield to which she accepts. Lyonel drafts Dunk and Egg to help in a tug-of-war game, which they win. Dunk sells his favorite horse Sweetfoot to buy new armor from blacksmith Steely Pate. Dunk and Egg watch the tournament's first jousting matches, which include Prince Valarr Targaryen and Lord Medgar Tully among the participants. Dunk realizes Arlan has no legacy because he achieved little in life, leaving Dunk despondent that he may end up the same.

| ShortSummary    = While Dunk sleeps, Egg trains the warhorse, Thunder. He is confronted by Ser Robyn Rhysling, who questions if the horse was stolen. Egg tells Dunk that only highborn knights compete on the tournament's first day. While Dunk buys food, Tanselle says his shield will be ready that evening. Egg requests to permanently squire for Dunk, but Plummer interrupts them. He privately asks Dunk to participate in a rigged joust against Ser Androw Ashford to recoup money spent on hosting the costly tournament. Dunk is baffled by the proposal. During a jousting match, Aerion acts dishonourably and mortally wounds Ser Humfrey Hardyng's horse, enraging the crowd. A fortune teller predicts that Egg will become king and die in flames. Dunk and Raymun discuss Aerion's jousting match, and Raymun expresses his disdain for the Targaryens. Egg watches Tanselle's performance of a dragon being slain. Feeling his family was insulted, Aerion breaks Tanselle's finger. Egg fetches Dunk, who becomes infuriated and attacks the prince. Guards quickly restrain Dunk as Aerion prepares to take revenge, but Egg orders them to stop and reveals that he and Aerion are brothers.

| ShortSummary    = Egg tells an imprisoned Dunk that his real name is Aegon Targaryen. He hid his identity to become a squire after his brother, Daeron, the belligerent drunk noble from the inn, refused to participate in the tournament. Baelor informs Dunk that Daeron has accused Dunk of kidnapping Egg. Dunk requests a trial by combat, but Aerion demands a trial by seven. Dunk must find six knights to fight beside him in a seven-versus-seven joust at dawn. Steffon agrees to fight for Dunk, and Egg says that Daeron, Maekar, and three Kingsguard will fight for Aerion. Daeron apologizes to Dunk and promises to intentionally fall from his horse. He privately tells Dunk about a prophetic dream of seeing Dunk with a dead dragon. Pate informs Dunk that Tanselle has fled Ashford and returned to Dorne, then gives him his shield and armor. As dawn breaks, Egg brings Lyonel, Robyn, Hardyng, and Ser Humfrey Beesbury, to fight for Dunk, but Steffon switches sides after Aerion promised him a lordship. Lyonel knights Raymun to replace Steffon. Still one knight short, Dunk appeals to the crowd's honor; Baelor declares that he will fight for Dunk.

| ShortSummary    = The trial of seven begins. In the first charge, Aerion knocks Dunk off his horse. In a series of flashbacks to Dunk's childhood, he and his friend Rafe scavenge from a battlefield. They return to Flea Bottom in King's Landing and pickpocket from Alester, a City Watchman. Dunk and Rafe attempt to buy passage to the Free Cities in Essos, but cannot afford it. Alester corners them and takes their money. Rafe steals Alester's dagger, but he notices and slits her throat. Arlan emerges from a tavern and kills Alester, saving Dunk, who then follows Arlan on his travels. In the present, Dunk duels Aerion on foot until both men collapse from injury. After Dunk falls unconscious, Aerion declares him dead. Egg begs Dunk to get up, and the crowd chants for Dunk as he stands. Dunk and Aerion resume their duel until Dunk gets the upper hand. Aerion yields and withdraws his accusation. In the aftermath, Beesbury and Hardyng are confirmed as killed. Dunk pledges fealty to Baelor. Raymun and Pate help Baelor remove his helmet, which Maekar struck with his mace during the trial, revealing a fatal wound. Baelor collapses from his injury and dies in Dunk's arms.

| ShortSummary    = Lyonel invites Dunk to Storm's End, but Dunk believes that he brings only bad luck. Baelor's body is cremated at his funeral. Dunk meets Valarr, who questions why his father died, but Dunk was left alive. Raymun reveals he has married the prostitute Red whose real name is Rowan. Maekar informs Dunk that Aerion will spend time in the Free Cities to atone. He laments that Baelor would have been a good king and invites Dunk to Summerhall and take Egg as his squire. Dunk declines, which Egg overhears. In a flashback, Dunk asks a dying Arlan why he was never knighted. Arlan retorts that a true knight always finishes a story. In the present, Daeron tells Dunk that he should mentor Egg lest he become like Aerion. Egg discovers that his hair is regrowing. He takes a knife to Aerion's bedroom, but Maekar calms him down. Dunk asks Maekar if Egg can squire for him on the road, which Maekar refuses. Raymun buys Sweetfoot back for Dunk, who then gifts her to Raymun. As Dunk leaves Ashford, Egg arrives, and they depart together. Egg suggests that they travel to Dorne. An angry Maekar later realizes that Egg is gone.

Production
Development
Casting
Writing
Filming
Reports about the possible filming of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms in Belfast (Northern Ireland) emerged in November 2023 after Lisa Byrne, producer of Game of Thrones since its third season, updated her LinkedIn profile, where she indicated her participation as line producer and listed Belfast as the filming location; the BBC confirmed this location in May 2024. Belfast also served as the main production center for Game of Thrones and hosted the filming of the pilot episode of a spin-off series starring Naomi Watts, a project that was ultimately not greenlit by HBO.
Filming began in Belfast on June 17, 2024, two weeks later than originally scheduled. Gustav Danielsson worked as cinematographer with Harris and Federico Cesca with Smith. Filming concluded on September 14, which Ansell celebrated with a video on Instagram. The series also incorporated part of the technical team that worked on Game of Thrones.
The interior scenes were filmed mainly at Titanic Studios, while the exterior sequences were shot at various locations in Northern Ireland. Part of the grounds of Glenarm Castle represented Ashford Meadow and Myra Castle (Strangford) represented Ashford Tournament Grounds; other filming locations used to recreate various locations in Ashford and the Reach included Cave Hill, Hidden Village of Galboly (both in Antrim) and Leitrim Lodge (Newry). The production also filmed scenes set in the Crownlands in Tollymore Forest Park (Bryansford); the Dark Hedges represented the King's Road. The crew also shot the scene in which Dunk buries Ser Arlan of Pennytree near Hen Mountain (Newry), where the production installed the elm tree that appears on screen. Game of Thrones used several of these locations, including Titanic Studios, the Mourne Mountains, Myra Castle, Glenarm Castle, Tollymore Forest Park, and the Dark Hedges.
A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms employed approximately 650 local crew members and hundreds of extras during filming in Northern Ireland, as well as hiring various regional companies for catering, construction, lighting, camera, and post-production services. Northern Ireland Screen estimated that the series generated an investment of £30 million for the local economy, and its chairman, Richard Williams, said they were "absolutely delighted" to learn that the series would be produced in Northern Ireland.
Music

Dan Romer composed the score for the television series, marking the first time a season of the franchise did not feature Ramin Djawadi in the role. Romer and Parker collaborated closely on the composition and shared ideas during production; they incorporated elements inspired by western music associated with Ennio Morricone, but sought to maintain the feeling that the music belongs to the Game of Thrones universe. According to Parker, the music needed to represent Dunk, so Romer opted for a sound with a "whimsy feeling". WaterTower Music digitally released an soundtrack album on February 22, 2026, featuring 22 tracks that compile the series' original music.
Parker sought to convey a sense of warmth through a cheerful, melodic, and deliberately unpolished score. Romer primarily used string instruments such as violins, cellos, and guitars, and created musical motifs associated with Dunk and Egg; scenes related to House Targaryen received a more classical and operatic musical treatment. Romer and Parker selected instruments consistent with the fourteenth century and avoided the use of modern instruments such as electric guitars or drums; Parker also limited the use of flutes, as David Benioff and D. B. Weiss "hated" them. Giosuè Greco, a frequent collaborator of Romer, performed the whistled melodies of the score.
The first episode includes the Game of Thrones main theme composed by Djawadi, which is used to represent the "call to greatness" that Dunk hears in his head; the theme reappears at the end of the fourth episode to indicate that this "call" persists. The sixth episode also incorporates the songs "Alone Together" by Kenny Dorham, used to reflect Dunk's pain and guilt, and "Sixteen Tons", performed by Tennessee Ernie Ford, a song about labor exploitation that alludes to Dunk's social status. The latter marked the first inclusion of a pre-existing song in the franchise's soundtrack, and contains references to Catholicism, a religion that does not exist in the fictional universe. After the episode aired, "Sixteen Tons" reached the second position among the most searched country songs on Shazam in the United States and eighth worldwide.

Design
Post-production
The series does not include an title sequence and instead uses an intertitle with "medieval-style" typography; Parker explained that this decision was intended to reflect Dunk's personality and differentiate the series from the elaborate openings of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon, although he acknowledged that dispensing with a title sequence was "probably the most stressful decision" he made on the series. Unlike House of the Dragon, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms made minimal use of computer-generated imagery.
Release
Broadcast and home media
world premiere was held at the Zoo Palast in Berlin, where the first two episodes were screened.]]
While the series was originally indicated to begin airing in late 2025, Bloys denied this in May 2025, clarifying that it would instead premiere in 2026, and in September he set the launch month for January. The first teaser trailer, released on October 9, revealed that the series would premiere in the United States on January 18, 2026. The season was broadcast on HBO in the United States, with each episode released simultaneously on HBO Max; it was also released on Crave in Canada, JioHotstar in India, U-NEXT in Japan, Neon in New Zealand, and Sky Group channels and Now in the United Kingdom and Ireland. Unlike Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon, which premiered their episodes on Sundays at 09:00 p. m. ET, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms aired at 10:00 p. m. ET, as that time slot was occupied by Industry (2020–present).
The first two episodes received their red carpet world premiere at the Zoo Palast in Berlin on January 13, followed by another red carpet premiere at the Cinema Moderno in Rome on January 15. Theater screenings of the first two episodes were held in the Netherlands on January 15, in London on January 16, and in Los Angeles on January 17. Behind-the-scenes videos titled Inside the Episode were released on HBO Max and YouTube after each episode, while HBO Max also released a weekly companion video podcast hosted by Jason Concepcion and Greta Johnsen featuring interviews with members of the cast and crew. The season was released digitally and on DVD, Blu-ray, and Ultra HD Blu-ray in the United Kingdom on June 15, and in the United States on June 16; a SteelBook edition was also made available in the United Kingdom. The home media release includes several behind-the-scenes featurettes, including Building A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, the web documentary series A Knight in the Making, and the Inside the Episode series.
Promotion
With the announcement on June 18, 2024, that filming had begun, HBO released the first image of Claffey in costume. The first footage of the series was revealed in a Max trailer during the second-season finale of House of the Dragon on August 4,​ featuring Claffey, Ansell, Vaughan-Lawlor, and Webb.​ This was followed by the release of the first still frame on October 5, 2025, and the first poster on October 6.​ The first teaser trailer premiered on October 9, after being presented at the show's panel at the New York Comic Con,​ which was attended by Claffey, Ansell, Parker, and Martin.​ Eleven additional image stills were released on December 3.​ Claffey and Ansell also attended the series' panel at CCXP on December 4,​ where the final trailer was released. The panel also featured a video message from Fabien Frankel and Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, who portrayed Ser Criston Cole in House of the Dragon and Jaime Lannister in Game of Thrones, respectively.
On January 12, 2026, Parker and Martin attended a fan-exclusive event organized by Thalia in collaboration with WBD at the Delphi Filmpalast am Zoo in Berlin, where they discussed the adaptation of books into television series. The event, titled "From Script to Screen", was sold out and attended by 700 people, and was followed by a book signing by Martin.​ Part of the cast and crew attended the HBO Max launch party in Berlin on January 13, which was immediately followed by the series' red carpet world premiere. A similar event took place in Rome on January 15, with cast and crew members attending the HBO Max launch party and the series' subsequent red carpet premiere.
HBO Max, in collaboration with the creative agency Armed Mind,​ launched the digital campaign Squire for Hire on January 29, 2026. The campaign consisted of three short-form videos released on social media at one-hour intervals, featuring an actor portraying a medieval-style squire assisting celebrities Noah Beck, Marshawn Lynch, and The Chainsmokers;​ it generated approximately 18 million organic views within just over a week without paid promotion. In conjunction with the campaign, HBO Max partnered with the home services platform Taskrabbit and launched the website squireforhire.com, which included a sweepstakes allowing fans to book the squire featured in the videos. Although the marketing campaign was described as "modest," several media outlets named A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms among their most anticipated television series of 2026.
Reception
Critical response
On review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms has an approval rating of 94% based on 165 critics' reviews. The website's general consensus reads, "A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms is a welcome return to Westeros that works better in the buddy-comedy arena rather than solely slaying its competition." Metacritic calculated a weighted average of 74 out of 100 based on 37 reviews, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.
Ratings
The series ranked ninth on ScreenShare's weekly list of most anticipated content for the period of January 3 to 9, where it surpassed Bridgerton (2020–present). By January 19, the series ranked fifth among the most-watched HBO programs worldwide, while on HBO Max it led trending charts in every country where the platform was available. The first episode drew 6.7 million viewers in the United States across its first three nights, combining linear viewership and HBO Max streams; this result placed it as HBO's third most-watched premiere within that timeframe. According to Samba TV, the production ranked third among the most-watched streaming programs during the week of January 19 to 25, held that position from January 26 to February 1, and rose to first place in the week of February 2 to 8. By late January, the series led HBO Max trends in the United States and ranked first or near the top in sixty-five international markets.
The series returned to ninth place on ScreenShare's list for the week of January 31 to February 6, reflecting "interest in the expanding Game of Thrones universe." The show registered demand 73.7 times higher than the average series in the United States, placing it "on par" with the first season of House of the Dragon; this figure made it the most successful debut of 2026 up to that point. Demand in the United Kingdom reached nearly two-thirds of that recorded in the United States, with similar performance in Canada, Northern Europe, and Australia. In the week of the fourth episode, from February 9 to 15, the series dropped to fourth place on Samba TV's list, before returning to the cusp in the week of February 16 to 22. By February 17, the series surpassed The Pitt (2025–present) and regained the top spot among HBO Max's global trends.
The final two episodes had 9.2 and 9.5 million viewers on their first three nights, a 37% and 42% increase from the premiere. By February 19, the first five episodes were averaging 13 million viewers across linear viewers and streams, surpassing The Pitts 12 million. By February 26, the six episodes averaged 14 million in the United States and 26 million globally, establishing the series as the third most successful debut season in HBO Max history, behind The Last of Us (2023–present) and House of the Dragon. During the week of February 21 to 27, the series rose to third place in ScreenShare's rankings, and ranked second on Samba TV's list for the period of February 23 to March 1. By March 15, it placed first on the Apple TV Store while holding second place on HBO Max. The series showed strong appeal among Generation Z and zillennials.
